audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings call Quinn's ultimate 'Behold, Harrier (R)' — whys[4], spikes[1] and mid, plus wants.foe[1]'s 'Harrier ult'.
audit.why: Her R is Behind Enemy Lines; Harrier is the passive mark, and Skystrike is the damage on ending the ability. Same class of fabricated name as 'Ares of Blaze' for Pyroclasm.
audit.corrected: Behind Enemy Lines (R), 700 range, ending it casts Skystrike and re-marks with Harrier.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Behind Enemy Lines is a channel Condemn cancels, and Vault is described as a knockback.
audit.why: The kit flags R as channel ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'), so a landed Condemn ends her roam or her dive on the spot. And Riot's Vault text is a 675-range dash that briefly interrupts the target and leaps her back to near max attack range — she does not knock you back, she removes herself.
audit.corrected: Behind Enemy Lines is a channel Condemn cancels; Vault is a 675 dash on 12s at rank 1 that leaps her off you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill, Quinn, Quinn, Skill, Skill, Quinn, Quinn; the audited Quinn side reads Quinn for rows 0-5 and Vayne at 2+ items.
audit.why: whys[0], whys[3] and whys[4] already describe Quinn winning those rows, and whys[6] describes Vayne taking the sidelane at two items — the chart is the only part disagreeing. Blinding Assault out-ranges Vayne 1025 to 550 for the whole laning phase.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 to Quinn and row 6 to Vayne as one atomic paired group.

audit.why: Four spikes, staged Lvl 3-5 / Lvl 6 / 1st item / Late, and the arc — her lane, her roam, her burst, then Vayne's two-item sidelane flip — matches the corrected chart exactly.

edits.before: Behold, Harrier (R) at 6 lets her dive or roam while you can't react.
edits.after: Behind Enemy Lines (R) at 6 lets her cross the map and dive you.

edits.before: Behold, Harrier (R) turns Quinn into a roaming demon; she can dive you or leave to snowball other lanes while your Final Hour does nothing for immobile you. Ward and respect the roam.
edits.after: Behind Enemy Lines turns Quinn into a roamer; she can dive you or leave to snowball other lanes. It is a channel, so a landed Condemn cancels it outright — ward and respect the roam.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are her window: Vault (E) knocks you back and resets her AA, and at 6 her Behold, Harrier ult lets her all-in or roam. Buy time and ward.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are her window: Vault (E) is a 675-range dash on 12s that leaps her off you, and at 6 Behind Enemy Lines lets her all-in or roam. Ward it.

edits.before: Roam with Harrier ult to snowball
AA-tumble-AA on Quinn's step-up, proc the third silver bolt for true damage, and walk away before he reaches you.
edits.after: Blinding Assault blinds you from 1025 range on an 11s cooldown at rank 1 — walk out of the zone, not through it.

edits.before: Quinn wastes Vault (Dash/Blind) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Vault dashes 675 on a 12s cooldown, then leaps her back off you.

edits.before: That is Quinn's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Her blind reaches out to 1025, and your entire pattern is auto-attacks.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Behind Enemy Lines is a channel — Condemn cancels it outright.

edits.before: - Quinn Vault: matchup-defining — Her engage + blind. Condemn the follow-up. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Blinding Assault: 11s at rank 1, 1025 range — it blinds your entire pattern. - Vault: 12s, a 675 dash that leaps off you. - Behind Enemy Lines: a channel Condemn cancels. - Final Hour: 100s.

notes: Worth knowing for the champion-level pass: Heightened Senses (W) is flagged revealsStealth and reveals a large area on a 50s cooldown at rank 1. That is a direct answer to Final Hour's Tumble invisibility, but the kit text says 'reveal a large area nearby' without stating whether the reveal actually strips Vayne's invisibility — I could not verify it, so no line on the page asserts it either way. Also inherited: several full-layer strings still call Vayne 'he/his'.
